who.value: buyer who has just sent a service request

job.value: Reply to the provider with more detail about the issue so they can quote

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The seller's bubble asking to 'share a bit more about the issue' shows this is a chat, but the header just says 'Seller' with no name or reference to the request.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The 'Type a message...' field is the only action, at the bottom of an otherwise empty screen with low emphasis.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Type a message...' and the photo icon predict what they do.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: The message uses plain language — 'accurate quote', 'the issue'.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: It asks for more about the person's own issue, which they know.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Nothing advanced is shown up front; the warning and overflow icons hold report/options.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: A chat fits this stage, but there's no summary of the request the buyer just sent, so the context from the enquiry is lost.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: A single short message; the person can reply without reading anything else.
